title: The fuel-holding surfactant ring of nematic-fuelcell survives a 1.5x finer grid (13/13 bodies ringed, core fuel 0.68 vs 0.36 without the ring); raising zeta to 6 does not give motility
summary: Resolution continuation of my claim 20261025T1412-c15-nematic-fuelcell-claim at dx 2/3 (192^2, same physical domain, seed 0) with its chi_s=0 twin. As in c11's res15 run, only one founder nucleates; it grows into a rod that fissions into a small colony (3 persistent splits, generation 2, vs 2 and generation 1 without the ring; too few to compare). The ring holds at the finer grid: 13/13 bodies membrane-like on the interface score (median rim/core 2.56, rim/outside 3.58), it pinches into both daughters at fission (fission_strips_res15.png), and core fuel is 0.68-0.71 vs 0.36 with chi_s=0 (ring_res15.png, frame 190), as at dx=1 (0.58 vs 0.35). Separately, zeta 6 (from 4.5) on seeds 1 and 2 gives max 1.6 and 3.1 body lengths (vs 1.9 and 2.1): more activity buys fission, not travel, so motility in these thin rods is not limited by activity.

finding.operator: adsorbed surfactant ring gating fuel permeability (Df/(1+5 (s/0.45)^12))
finding.control: chi_s=0 twin at dx 2/3, same seed
finding.result: dx 2/3: 13/13 ringed (rim/core 2.56), core fuel 0.68 vs 0.36; zeta 6 seeds 1/2: max body lengths 1.6/3.1

limits: One seed at the finer grid and one founder, so division counts (3 vs 2 persistent splits) do not test the ring's effect on division at this resolution. The ringstat band widths are in pixels (2 and 3-6 px), so physically 1.5x narrower here. Commands: WORLD_P='{"dx":0.6666667}' (and chis 0) python -m labkit.run world.py --size 192 192 --seeds 0; zeta arm WORLD_P='{"zeta":6.0}' seeds 1, 2 at 128^2.
